assessment.nobel_worthiness: Incretin physiology to GLP-1 receptor agonists is a rare chain from basic hormone biology (proglucagon processing, glucose-dependent insulin secretion, satiety and gastric effects) to therapies transforming type 2 diabetes and obesity, with clear cardiometabolic outcome benefits. Originality, clarity and lasting impact are all very high.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology of GLP-1 and its insulinotropic action) and Drucker (GLP-1 and GLP-2 biology, therapeutic translation) are central to the science; Knudsen led the design of long-acting acylated analogues (liraglutide, semaglutide) that made the drug class. Mojsov's contribution (identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1 peptide) is credited in the list but disputed in the wider record, and Habener is not in the supplied names. The three-person configuration is defensible but contested.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation through large randomized outcome trials and widespread clinical use; the field is stable and recognition is timely, arguably pressing.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among Holst, Drucker, Mojsov, Knudsen and others is contested; I am relying on my own recollection and have not verified the details.
Whether a prize should recognize basic physiology, peptide chemistry or drug development, or combine them, is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells as living drugs produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell leukemias and lymphomas and opened a new therapeutic modality; conceptual originality and clinical consequence are high.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (early second-generation CARs with costimulation), June (clinical translation of CD19 CAR-T with 4-1BB) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer and TIL/gene-engineered lymphocytes) form a plausible three-way split. Eshhar and others who made first-generation CAR concepts are not in the supplied names, which limits the fairness of the configuration.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and years of follow-up confirm efficacy in hematologic cancers; limited efficacy in solid tumors, toxicity and cost remain, but the core discovery is mature.
uncertainties: Priority among CAR design pioneers is not fully captured by the supplied names.
Solid-tumor impact is unproven; I have not independently verified clinical details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience millisecond, cell-type-specific control of activity, transforming causal circuit dissection across species from invertebrates to primates. Its methodological impact on the study of motor, sensory and affective circuits is exceptional and foundational.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann identified and characterized channelrhodopsins as light-gated channels; Deisseroth led the adaptation to neurons and behavior in mammals. Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenböck made early and important contributions, so any three-person set leaves out major figures and credit is hard to allocate.
assessment.maturity: Widely used and independently reproduced for roughly two decades; recognition is timely. Clinical translation (retinal optogenetics) is emerging but is not required for the discovery's maturity.
uncertainties: Which three of six credited individuals is genuinely the fairest set is unresolved.
This is a tool rather than a disease mechanism, which may matter for the Medicine prize framing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new mode of organelle-to-nucleus signaling, with IRE1 splicing of HAC1/XBP1 and a transcriptional program controlling ER capacity. It is conceptually original, clear and relevant to diabetes, neurodegeneration, cancer and secretory-cell physiology.
assessment.attribution: Mori (identification of the UPR transcriptional response and the pathway components) and Walter (IRE1 as the sensor, unconventional mRNA splicing, ISR and ISRIB work) are the natural and compact pair; both appear in the supplied credit. Credit is cleaner than for most candidates.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism has been confirmed for decades across yeast and mammals; therapeutic exploitation is still early, but the discovery is mature and stable.
uncertainties: Direct disease-treatment impact is still limited.
Contributions of others in the early ER-stress field (e.g., Kaufman, Ron) are not in the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mechanism-guided antisense correction of SMN2 splicing led to nusinersen, which changed the natural history of spinal muscular atrophy, a fatal childhood motor neuron disease; it also validated splice-modulating oligonucleotides as a general platform.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing regulatory mechanism and ASO design for SMN2 exon 7 inclusion) and Bennett (antisense chemistry and drug development) form a natural two-person pairing. Contributions by Hua, Singh and clinical trial investigators are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with long-term clinical follow-up and extended use of the ASO platform; maturity is good, though the discovery is more recent than others.
uncertainties: Splitting credit between mechanistic RNA biology and chemistry/drug development is a judgment call.
Gene therapy and small-molecule alternatives for SMA may affect perception of uniqueness.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: cGAS-STING defines how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immunity through the second messenger cGAMP, linking infection, autoimmunity, senescence and tumor immunity. The discovery is original, mechanistically clear and broadly consequential.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and cGAMP as the DNA sensor and second messenger, and Barber discovered STING; the pair covers the decisive steps. Others (Ishikawa and Barber on STING, Sun and Wu on cGAS in Chen's lab) are credited, but Chen with Barber is the cleaner configuration. Related work by others (e.g., on cyclic dinucleotides) is not in the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Mechanistic findings are broadly replicated; therapeutic translation (STING agonists and antagonists) has not yet delivered approved drugs, so clinical maturity is incomplete.
uncertainties: Credit for STING discovery involves several groups, and the supplied list may not fully reflect that.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR/mTOR as the central controller of growth in response to nutrients and growth factors links metabolism to cell growth, aging, cancer and immunosuppression; the discovery is foundational and widely applied.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR in yeast and defined its core biology, while Sabatini identified mammalian mTOR and the nutrient-sensing arms (mTORC1 regulation, Rag GTPases). Schreiber's contribution through rapamycin/FKBP12 chemistry is also important, so the allocation is not fully settled; Brown, Sabatini and Snyder cloned mTOR/FRAP at about the same time.
assessment.maturity: Extremely well replicated and stable across systems; clinical use of rapalogs is established but the full therapeutic potential is still being explored.
uncertainties: Allocation between Hall, Sabatini and Schreiber, and exclusion of other early mTOR cloners, is uncertain.
Recent controversies surrounding one credited person may affect committee deliberation; I cannot verify them.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-term potentiation provided the first widely accepted synaptic cellular model of memory and made synaptic plasticity experimentally tractable. Its conceptual influence on neuroscience is large, and NMDA receptor-dependent LTP became a core framework.
assessment.attribution: Bliss and Lømo reported the 1973 discovery of LTP in the rabbit hippocampus, and Collingridge showed NMDA receptor dependence. Morris's spatial-learning work tests the link to memory and is also credited, so a three-person set omits a significant figure.
assessment.maturity: The phenomenon is thoroughly replicated, but its precise relation to learning and memory in vivo remains debated, and clinical translation is minimal, which weakens its maturity relative to other candidates.
uncertainties: Causal link between LTP and memory storage remains debated.
Choice between Collingridge and Morris for the third position is uncertain.
